newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan executed in public in tit-for-tat sentence.
newsitem.headline: Afghan executed in public in tit-for-tat sentence.

text.p: A man convicted of murder by an Islamic court was publicly executed by a relative of his four victims on Friday in the western Afghan city of Herat, a senior Afghan official said.

Tens of thousands of people watched the execution of the 35-year-old convict, Shakar (one name), at the sports stadium of the city, which is controlled by the Islamic Taleban militia, Herat governor Mullah Yar Mohammad told Reuters by telephone.

He said Shakar was found guilty of killing two men and two women of a family two months ago in a feud. The Islamic tit-for-tat sentence was carried out after Talaban leader Mullah Mohammad Omar rejected a clemency appeal and the family of the dead also declined to pardon the convict or accept blood money.
A relative of the dead, invited to carry out the punishment, fired four Kalashnikov rounds into Shakar's head, the governor said.
"People had come to see the execution of God's will," he said. "They were impressed."

Friday's was the third public execution in Herat since the city was captured in September last year by the Taleban, which now controls more than two-thirds of the country, including the capital of Kabul.
